disposition_reason: Twenty Greek walnut oils (10 conventional, 10 organic) were analysed by ICP-AES; Table 5 prints per-sample values for Ca, Fe, Mg and Zn and reports cadmium, lead and nine other elements as not detected in every sample.

study.design: Method development and validation with real-sample comparison of conventional vs organic walnut oils
study.origin: Chandler variety walnuts from Thessaly, Greece; oil obtained by mechanical extraction
study.market: not purchased at retail; authentic samples from producers
study.method: Pressure-assisted Teflon autoclave digestion with HNO3, ICP-AES
study.qa: BCR 278-R (mussel tissue) recoveries e.g. Cd 95.1%, Pb 94.5%; spiked walnut oil recoveries 85.0-110.2%

controls.control: Organic vs conventional farming of walnuts
controls.outcome: Fe and Zn no significant difference (p > 0.05); Ca and Mg significantly higher in organic oils (p < 0.05); Cd and Pb not detected in either

unresolved: The text says mercury was not determined in any sample, but mercury is not among the elements in the method or Table 5; no Hg finding recorded.
Detection limits for cadmium (1.53 ug/g) and lead (2.43 ug/g) are high relative to typical oil levels, so non-detects are weak evidence of low contamination.
Mg in CWO8 and OWO7 printed nd in Table 5 while the text says Mg ranged from <LOQ; recorded as printed (nd).
